title: Agent tools: seven private modules plus registration

details.goal: Answer is the graph current and what does it cover, including for paths that were never indexed.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'status', description: the verbatim text from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 2, profile:'agent'} and input {paths: array of string optional, budget: integer default 800}. handler.ts exports handle(ctx, args) returning handle(env) built only via constructors from #shared/envelope and sized only via #shared/budget emit. Reads: meta for project_name, project_root, generation, indexed_at, indexer_state, consecutive_failures; latest generation row; file rows plus not_indexed rows for each requested path using prefix ranges; census by language derived from file.parse_status and not_indexed.language. Payload keys exactly: project{name,root,commit,db_path}, graph{nodes,edges,size_bytes,db_path}, languages[{language,files,parsed,failed,note?}], paths[{path,indexed,symbols?,sha256?,reason?}], health{indexer,last_publish_ms,consecutive_failures}. A requested path with no file row and no not_indexed row must appear with indexed:false and reason not_indexed_unknown. This tool owns no other module and imports only #shared/*.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the description and input schema
Write handler.ts reading meta, generation, file and not_indexed
Build the languages census merging file rows and not_indexed rows
Build the per-path result including the unknown-path case
Write handler.test.ts against a fake reader covering complete coverage, a skipped path and an unknown path
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-status.test.ts && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun x tsc --noEmit. Done when the three cases return status ok, the envelope has all nine fields, and a grammar-unavailable language appears with parsed 0 and a note.

details.goal: One free-text input returns the resolved symbol and its neighbours grouped by relation, with a working resume path.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'trace', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 3, profile:'agent'} and input {query: string required, direction: enum all|in|out default all, kinds: array optional, depth: integer default 2 min 1 max 4, budget: integer default 3200, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts: first, if args.cursor is present, call ctx.cursor.verify(cursor, {tool:'trace', argsHash, generation}) where argsHash covers every other argument; on cursor_invalid, cursor_expired or cursor_mismatch return envelope fail with that code and the hint re-run the original call — never return a partial page. On ok, resume from the decoded position instead of starting at the first item. Then resolve via #shared/domain/resolve; on ambiguous return envelope ambiguous with up to 5 candidates and no payload body; on not_found return not_found with near_misses; on ok call #shared/domain/neighbors expand and shape the payload. Payload keys exactly: resolution{query,matched,kind,how,confidence}, node{id,qn,kind,file,lines,signature,is_test}, in[] and out[] as arrays of {edge,tier,items[{id,qn,kind,file,line,hop,external?,is_test?}]}, unresolved[{file,line,name,evidence,tier}], not_indexed[]. Groups ordered calls, inherits, implements, references, tested_by, imports — the order is fixed and empty groups are omitted. Pass the payload to emit(env, args.budget, {mint: position => ctx.cursor.sign({generation, tool:'trace', argsHash, position})}) so truncation produces a resumable next. Never include source text.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the description and the six-argument input schema
Write handler.ts: verify and apply an incoming cursor before any work
Wire resolve then expand
Shape grouped neighbours with tier hoisted to the group and the fixed group order
Attach unresolved and not_indexed from coverage assemble, then call emit with the mint callback
Write tests/tools-trace.test.ts covering ok, ambiguous, not_found and a truncated page resumed by cursor
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-trace.test.ts. Done when a unique name returns grouped neighbours with hop and tier, a two-candidate query returns ambiguous without a payload, an unresolved call site in scope yields total_relation gte, and a truncated response's next cursor returns the following page with no duplicates.

tasks.title: Tool module: summary (change, repo, area scopes)

details.goal: The hottest path: a few hundred tokens that say what changed, how risky it is and what to call next.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'summary', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 4, profile:'agent'} and input {scope: enum change|repo|area default change, target: string optional, base: string optional defaulting to the generation base_commit, budget: integer default 1200, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts dispatches on scope and must not compute repo or area aggregates on the change path. change payload keys: base, changed_files[], changed_symbols[{id,qn,kind,change,lines,risk}], risk{score,band,drivers[]}, test_gaps[{qn,reason}], removed_symbols[], suggested_next[{tool,query?,why}]. repo payload keys: size{files,nodes,edges}, languages[], entry_points[{qn,kind,reachable}], coupling_hotspots[{qn,in,out}], flows[{name,steps,files}], not_indexed[]. area payload keys: target, surface[{qn,kind}], dependents_total, risk. risk.drivers are sentences such as 41 dependents or 2 changed symbols without tests, never a bare float.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the scope enum and the five-argument schema
Implement the change path using diff changedSince plus metrics for risk
Implement the repo path using census, entry points by is_entry and hotspots by degree
Implement the area path using prefix range files and their dependents
Write handler.test.ts asserting all three scopes return their documented keys and that suggested_next names only real tools
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-summary.test.ts. Done when the three scopes return exactly their documented payload keys, the change scope reports driver sentences, and a stale generation sets read_status.stale true without failing the call.

details.goal: Find a declaration when the caller knows roughly what it is called but not where it lives.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'search', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 5, profile:'agent'} and input {query: string required, kind: enum function|method|class|file|decorator optional, path: string optional prefix filter, budget: integer default 2000, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts runs an FTS5 MATCH against node_fts through raw sqlite on the injected reader connection (FTS5 is not modeled by Drizzle), joins node and node_metrics for degree, applies the optional kind and path filters, and breaks score ties by in_degree then id so pagination is stable. Payload keys: mode ('bm25' always in MVP), results[{id,qn,kind,file,lines,signature?,degree{in,out},score}]. Payload must report mode bm25 so a caller knows no semantic rerank happened. No source text in results.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the description and five-argument schema
Implement the FTS5 MATCH query through the raw connection with kind and path filters
Join node_metrics for degree and order by score then in_degree then id
Set mode to bm25 in the payload
Write handler.test.ts asserting ranking, the path filter and stable ordering across two identical calls
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-search.test.ts. Done when an exact name ranks first, a path prefix filter excludes everything outside it, and two identical calls return byte-identical result order.

tasks.title: Tool module: impact (blast radius for a change set)

details.goal: Say what a change can reach, how far away it is, through which edge, and whether it is tested.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'impact', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 6, profile:'agent'} and input {paths: array of string optional defaulting to the working-tree diff, base: string optional, depth: integer default 2 min 1 max 4, budget: integer default 2500, cursor: string optional}. handler.ts: change set from args.paths or #shared/domain/diff changedSince; expand inbound from those nodes to depth; attach per node tested_depth and is_entry from node_metrics. Payload keys: changed[{path,symbols,entry_point}], impacted[{id,qn,kind,hop,via,tier,tested,entry_point?}], unmatched_files[{path,reason}], risk{score,band,drivers[]}. A changed file with no nodes must appear in unmatched_files with reason, never be dropped silently. Total relation is gte whenever the impacted list is truncated or unresolved rows exist in scope.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the description and five-argument schema
Resolve the change set from paths or the diff and map files to nodes
Expand inbound to the requested depth attaching hop, via and tier
Attach tested and entry_point from node_metrics and collect unmatched_files
Write handler.test.ts covering a clean tree, an explicit path set and a file with no nodes
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-impact.test.ts. Done when a changed markdown file appears in unmatched_files, impacted rows carry hop and via, and a truncated result sets total_relation gte with a next cursor.

details.goal: One address for detail, so the other five tools never need detail_level or per-item flags.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'expand', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 7, profile:'agent'} and input {target: string required, what: enum members|edges|source|coverage optional, budget: integer default 2500}. handler.ts resolves target as an id, qn or path; infers what by kind when absent (file or class to members, function or method to edges, folder to coverage) and echoes the choice in payload.what plus payload.why as a sentence such as inferred: class -> members. Payload always includes target{id,qn,kind,lines}. members returns members[{id,name,kind,lines,degree}]; edges returns the grouped neighbour shape of trace for one node; coverage returns file and not_indexed rows for the path prefix; source returns a line window read from disk after verifying sha256 against file.sha256, setting source_drift true on mismatch instead of returning stale text.
steps: Write manifest.ts with the description and three-argument schema
Implement target resolution across id, qn and path
Implement the kind-to-what inference table and echo what plus why
Implement members, edges and coverage payloads
Implement the source window with sha256 verification and the source_drift flag
Write handler.test.ts covering inference for three kinds and the drift case
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-expand.test.ts. Done when a class target infers members, a method target infers edges, a folder target infers coverage, and a source request on a modified file returns source_drift true with no content.

details.goal: Expose a repair path without letting the agent profile see it, and without ever indexing inside the server process.
details.contract: manifest.ts exports manifest {name:'index', description verbatim from TOOLS-SPEC.md section 8, profile:'admin'} and input {force: boolean default false, mode: enum full|fast default full}. handler.ts spawns the worker process with Bun.spawn running bin/codegraph.ts worker, passes repoRoot and dataDir, streams the child stderr into the logger, and returns published counts from the child's final JSON line on stderr. It must never import #indexer or open a writer in-process. Exit codes map to envelope: 0 ok with payload{mode,duration_ms,previous_generation,files{scanned,parsed,failed,skipped}}, 2 ok with summary nothing to do, 75 fail with code index_locked and a hint naming the lock file, 1 fail internal with the child's last error line.
steps: Write manifest.ts with profile admin and the two-argument schema
Implement Bun.spawn of the worker with repoRoot and dataDir
Parse the child's final JSON line and map the four exit codes to envelopes
Write tests/tools-index.test.ts with a stubbed worker command covering exit 0, 2 and 75
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-index.test.ts. Done when the three exit codes map to ok, ok with nothing-to-do and fail with index_locked respectively, and the handler never writes to the database directly.

tasks.title: Register the seven tools in the composition root with profiles

details.goal: Make the server surface exactly seven tools with profiles, a live watcher, clean shutdown and wired next_tools.
details.contract: src/index.ts imports the seven manifests explicitly (no directory scanning), builds ToolContext {reader, cursor, log, now, config}, registers with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer using registerTool with the manifest description and a JSON Schema produced from the manifest input, and MUST ALSO: (1) select the profile from CODEGRAPH_PROFILE (default agent) where agent registers six tools and admin registers all seven, with the same selector driving the tools/list response; (2) start the watcher by calling startWatch imported relatively from ./indexer/watch.ts — a root-only import, never through #shared and never from a tool — when running mcp mode and CODEGRAPH_NO_WATCH is unset, keeping the handle so the exit path calls stop(); (3) install SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers that stop the watcher, release the write lock and close the database; (4) populate next_tools on every response from nextToolsFor(tool) imported from #shared/instructions; (5) wire the open-time guard from DATABASE.md section 5 (root_mismatch as a stale_reason, wrong_project_db, unsupported_filesystem, schema_too_new as refusals); (6) catch every handler throw into envelope fail with an AppError code, mapping budget_too_large and index_locked through unchanged. Must never write to stdout. index and status modes run the CLI equivalents and exit.
steps: Import the seven manifests and build the shared ToolContext once at startup
Register each tool with registerTool plus its JSON Schema and select the profile from CODEGRAPH_PROFILE
Start the watcher via a relative ./indexer/watch.ts import in mcp mode and wire SIGINT/SIGTERM to stop it, release the lock and close the db
Populate next_tools from nextToolsFor for every response
Implement the open-time guard and map handler throws to envelope fail with the AppError code
Write tests/mcp-surface.test.ts asserting two JSON-RPC responses, six agent-profile names, seven admin names and zero non-JSON stdout lines
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/mcp-surface.test.ts. Done when the test captures exactly two JSON-RPC responses (initialize then tools/list), the agent profile lists six names, CODEGRAPH_PROFILE=admin lists seven, and the non-JSON stdout line count is 0.

tasks.title: Phase 2 closing gate: seven tools over MCP against a real generation

details.goal: Prove the registered surface behaves as specified against a published database, not a fake reader.
details.contract: tools-smoke.test.ts indexes a small fixture repo through the worker into a temp data dir, then drives the real MCP server over stdio: initialize, tools/list (expect 6 names for the agent profile), then one tools/call per tool with arguments from TOOLS-SPEC.md. Assertions: every response parses as JSON-RPC and carries the nine envelope fields; status reports the generation; summary scope change returns base and risk; trace on a known function returns a resolution block; search ranks the exact name first; impact returns impacted rows or an explicit empty with total_relation eq; expand on a class id returns members; the index tool is absent from the agent profile list. Stdout must contain only JSON-RPC lines. This task owns no source files.
steps: Write tests/tools-smoke.test.ts driving the stdio server
Index the fixture through the worker before the calls
Assert tools/list is 6 and every envelope has nine fields
Assert per-tool payload keys from TOOLS-SPEC.md
Assert strictly non-JSON stdout lines are zero
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/tools-smoke.test.ts. Done when all seven tools respond within their budgets, the agent profile lists exactly 6, and the non-JSONRPC stdout line count is 0.
